A.why: Restrained charcoal/crimson/bone palette, clean fit, but from ARPG a flat dark robe block with no gown outline or headpiece.
A.fix: Add a pale or amber hood band and widen the hem past the sleeve cuffs so the skirt and head read from above.

B.why: Clearest gown/habit silhouette (fitted waist, full A-line to floor); amber wimple band reads from above; violet stole and stained-glass pendant on theme.
B.fix: Soften the ziggurat stair-step skirt tiers into fewer, taller flaring panels.

C.why: Candle-crown veil is the best invention of the run and reads from above, but the body is a stacked plinth with no waist; cyan accent off-palette.
C.fix: Rebuild the lower body: narrow the waist, drop the hip shelf, one smooth skirt flare.

D.why: Stained-glass window bodice and steeple hat are beautiful and on theme, but the skirt is a column in profile and the glass is hidden from the top camera.
D.fix: Flare the skirt front and back, and repeat stained-glass colour on top-facing surfaces.

E.why: Great-helm headpiece reads as iron armour; the skirt is a hollow slate box or tray, visible from above.
E.fix: Replace the plinth with a closed flaring skirt and the bucket helm with a veil.

F.why: Best top-down colour read (violet front panel and back bow); ideal palette with a bone collar; but it reads as a priest's cassock with a near-column skirt.
F.fix: Flare the skirt at the knee and swap the biretta for a veiled coif to feminise.

notes: No candidate fully solves both brief demands: a feminine, full-skirted gown and a strong top-down read at night. B has the best gown silhouette, F the best colour read from above, D the best stained-glass motif, C the best headpiece (candle crown). Combining C's candle crown or D's glass panel with B's skirt would be strongest. Keep B, F, D.
